dedupe_keys.name: 2020 census redistricting data public law 94 171 summary files

description: The P.L. 94-171 Redistricting Data Summary Files are the first detailed 2020 Census product, which the U.S. Census Bureau must deliver to every state under Public Law 94-171 of 1975 for legislative redistricting. They contain, for every census block and all higher geographies, total population, voting-age population, race and Hispanic origin, housing units by occupancy status (occupied or vacant) and group quarters population by major type (for example nursing facilities, correctional facilities, college housing, military quarters). Coverage: the 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, census day 1 April 2020; the legacy-format files were posted for FTP download on 12 August 2021 and the same data on data.census.gov on 16 September 2021. 2010 and 2000 redistricting files are also listed. Format and access: legacy-format pipe-delimited summary files by state with Microsoft Access shells and SAS and R import scripts, data.census.gov and the Census Data API (free key); free and public domain. Caveats: disclosure avoidance adds noise below the state level except to total population and housing unit counts; block values for small groups are unreliable. Simulation uses: the finest official population and housing unit counts, used to allocate exposure to hazard footprints, estimate customers per network node, and locate group-quarters populations for evacuation planning. Related records: the 2020 Census DHC, TIGER/Line blocks and boundaries, the Census Geocoder (which gives group quarters assistance) and address count listing files.
